# Calyra

*Eldest of the Grove*

## Personality

Patient and dry-humoured, she lets everyone finish speaking before she answers, and her answers are short. She still corrects students' spellwork out of habit.

## Lore

Calyra taught at the Grove School for forty years, and she has never quite stopped. She is seventy-four now and Eldest of the Grove, but she still corrects students' spellwork out of habit, sometimes in the middle of a Council meeting, sometimes in the middle of someone else's lesson. She is patient and dry-humoured, she lets everyone finish speaking before she answers, and her answers are short. Her former students say the shortness is the point: she has always believed that most people already know the answer, and only need to be left enough quiet to hear it.

### The teacher

Calyra came to the Grove School at twenty-five to teach the youngest students the first, simplest magic: how to listen to the forest before asking anything of it. She taught that and a dozen other things for forty years, and a remarkable number of the forest's teachers learned from her. Amaryl, who now teaches the coaxing of living wood, was one of her students, and still sometimes calls her "teacher" in Council by mistake. Calyra never corrects that particular mistake.

Nine years ago, when old Eldest Ferris died, the forest's teachers and elders gathered to choose from among themselves who would lead the Grove Council. Two names were spoken most often, Calyra's and Thessaly's, and Calyra won by a handful of voices. Thessaly took it graciously and has been Calyra's sharpest critic and most reliable ally ever since. Calyra would not want it any other way; she says a council with no Thessaly in it would agree itself off a cliff.

### The Heart Tree

Calyra leads the Grove Council from the Heart Tree. Ilwen, her steward, keeps the Council's records and greets every visitor on the stair, and she has been trying for two years to make him take a holiday. Isaura, who keeps the old Magician records, is her confidante, and the two of them talk late into the night in a room of the Heart Tree where nobody else is allowed to bring a lantern. Halcy, among the first of the Children of the Tree to settle in the forest, is her friend, and Calyra sometimes asks Halcy for advice over a basket of flowers, because Halcy notices things about the forest that its oldest Magicians have long since stopped seeing. Calyra has never married. Her students were her family, and the forest is her house.

### The friend from the highlands

Forty-seven years ago, in Calyra's third year of teaching, a young Brenna envoy named Odda got lost on the Lantern Paths after dark in her first week in the forest. Calyra found her sitting under a lantern pretending she had meant to stop there, and walked her home without teasing her once that night. She has teased her about it ever since.

Odda stayed three winters. She taught Calyra Brenna bonesetting and the uses of highland herbs, and Calyra taught her forest plant-lore and how to read the oldest Magician script. Every spring since, Odda has written a letter ahead and then come to the forest herself a few weeks later, carrying a bundle of highland herbs, and gone home with forest herbs for the Brenna healers. Odda leads the Brenna now, and Calyra thinks the highlands are lucky to have her. Odda thinks Calyra has been telling people what to do since she was twenty-seven, and Calyra cannot honestly deny it. The spring visit is the one week of the year when Calyra sets the Council aside entirely.

### Her quiet worry

Calyra's quiet worry is the seal scholars. Since the expedition damaged the seal fifty years ago, the forest's scholars have studied the old records day and night, trying to understand how it might be strengthened. Isaura leads them, and Calyra watches them sleep too little and find too little. She fears they will burn themselves out before they find anything, and she fears, even more privately, that there may be nothing in the records to find.

A quest might bring a missing spring letter from Odda, help the Council persuade an exhausted scholar to rest, or carry something from Isaura's records that Calyra does not want anyone else to read.
